newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay sugar prices see gains, low consumer demand.
newsitem.headline: Bombay sugar prices see gains, low consumer demand.

text.p: Bombay sugar prices on Wednesday gained, though consumer demand remained slow, with limited supplies and rising mill delivery firming prices, dealers said.
Sugar ready delivery moved up by 10 rupees at 1,475/1,510 rupees per quintal for the S-30 variety and at 1,495/1,535 rupees per quintal for the M-30 variety.
Local millers are witnessing higher offtake by neighbouring states which in turn curtailed supplies of sugar from mills to the Bombay market.
"Reports that the Indian government is considering a proposal to buy sugar from the open market to improve supplies at the public distribution system also aided the firm tendency," one broker said.
In the mill delivery sugar S-30 rose by five rupees at 1,410/1,420 rupees per quintal and M-30 rose by five rupees at 1,430/1,440 rupees per quintal.
